Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Tim Easterby who won over 5f on Good at Thirsk last time and steps up to 6f, which looks a natural progression; Duran Fentiman takes the ride and the stable is in strong form (T14: 8/68), making this a key player off a 16-day turnaround.
runners_data.comment: Lairy Mary was fourth last time out, and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Sixteen days on from that latest run, she takes her place mid-pack on our figures, the mixed form since that win the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Trust Havana
runners_data.note: Consistent run of below-par finishes (8th, 10th, 6th) on Good and Soft suggests limited scope for improvement; by nature a true hold-up horse who has been placed into midfield on the map, meaning Gary Hanmer's runner will struggle to find natural cover in a bunched, slowly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Trust Havana was sixth last time out, having also finished eighth two starts back and unplaced three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts and second-bottom on our figures, she has plenty to find after a 27-day break.

runners_data.name: Bea Kindly
runners_data.note: Modest form figures of 9-6-9 on Good ground over 5f tell a sobering story, and 69 days off the track for Tracy Waggott's runner adds an unknown element; her natural tendency to race deep into the field sits awkwardly in a race where genuine closers are starved of pace to run at.
runners_data.comment: Bea Kindly was ninth last time out and ninth again three starts back, with a sixth in between two starts back. She has run over today's trip and going before, but is yet to win in recent starts and returns from a lengthy 69-day absence to sit mid-pack on our figures.

runners_data.name: Spirit of Mary
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's two-year-old showed a glimmer with a third on Good at 6f but has run poorly at 5f and over Soft, suggesting this trip and ground are ideal conditions; placed into midfield by redistribution but is naturally a hold-up type, so Aiden Brookes will need to find a gap in what could be a compressed finish.
runners_data.comment: Spirit of Mary was third last time out, though well below that four starts back in ninth. She has run over today's trip and going before, but is yet to win in recent starts and sits bottom of our figures in this twelve-runner field, with plenty to find on her official mark too.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears runner has genuine hold-up credentials and a legitimate third-placed effort over 5f on Good last time for Harry Russell; not redistributed, so races closer to its natural position, and represents one of the more credible closers in the field if anything quickens the pace fractionally.
runners_data.comment: Enemy Action was third last time out, following an unplaced run two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts, he's a leading danger on figures after a 20-day break, with the unplaced effort in that sequence the main concern.

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's runner shows a form string of 5-3-6-6 on Good and Standard ground with no wins, and its natural hold-up style has been pushed forward on the map; Ethan Tindall takes a 5lb claim but the horse's record offers little encouragement that it can overcome a tactical mismatch in a steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: Claret And Blues was sixth last time out and sixth again two starts back, though he did finish third three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts, he sits mid-pack on our figures 17 days on.

runners_data.name: Liveadream
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's two-year-old ran well for second over 7f on Good and has shown ability at a longer trip, suggesting 6f may be on the sharp side; Sam James rides and while naturally a hold-up type displaced into midfield, the shorter distance and lack of genuine pace may work against a horse that has only shown at 7f.
runners_data.comment: Liveadream was runner-up last time out, having finished fourth two starts back and seventh three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts and towards the foot of our figures, she returns after a 32-day break.

runners_data.name: Crystal Kraken
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan's mount for Dylan Cunha carries a prominent racing style and a course-relevant third over 6f on Good, though its wins have come on Standard surfaces and this is its best going form in only one comparable run; a reliable position just off Lady Dublin would suit if the pace is steady.
runners_data.comment: Crystal Kraken was fifth last time out but had been third two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts, she returns from a 50-day absence to take her place mid-pack on our figures, that lengthy layoff the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, Jake Dickson (7) rides for Ollie Pears, who also trains Enemy Action; her winning run over 6f on Good here last time (just 9 days ago) is directly relevant, and she wears a hood (hg:p) which suggests a settled, front-running temperament — this is her race to lose.
runners_data.comment: Lady Dublin won last time out and was third two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going in the book. Just nine days on, she rates the one to beat on figures despite a below-par sixth three starts back.

runners_data.name: Eevee Star
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's runner carries a tongue-tie (hg:t) and has three runs showing a best of third over 6f on Good — the form is modest but consistent; Ryan Sexton rides and as a genuine hold-up type (not redistributed), her chance depends on something materialising in the final furlong that a slow pace makes unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Third of twelve on our figures and one of the dangers, Eevee Star has today trip and going experience plus a third among her recent runs. Two fifths in her latest starts and no win to her name are the queries, but the rating keeps her prominent 21 days on.

runners_data.name: Inns And Out
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's second runner in the race for Jason Hart showed a solid third over 6f on Good and comes back from 29 days off; a hold-up horse whose best position in this race is tracking the midfield pack, and Hart's course familiarity is worth a note in a race where positioning in the straight matters.
runners_data.comment: Inns And Out was sixth last time out having been third two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts, he's one of the leading dangers on figures after a 29-day break, that lack of a win the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner for Mark Winn has two third-placed efforts over 6f on Good and is equipped with a hood (hg:h); back after just 9 days and clearly fit, with strong course-going form (4/5 on Good), and of all the hold-up horses in this field appears most likely to produce a competitive late effort if the field spreads wide.
runners_data.comment: Mardy Bum was third last time out and third again two starts back, with experience over today's distance already banked. Yet to win in recent starts and towards the foot of our figures in this twelve-runner field, she's back just nine days on still seeking that elusive win.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Dublin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 2yo nursery handicap over 6f at Thirsk, and with no genuine pace rival to pressure her from the gates, she is likely to establish a comfortable, controlled lead at a sustainable tempo on Good ground. Lairy Mary and Crystal Kraken are the only horses with any prominent profile to track her, but neither is a natural front-runner, so Lady Dublin should dictate terms unopposed and set a rhythm that suits horses who can travel on the bridle behind her rather than those needing a fierce pace to close into. The large hold-up contingent — Trust Havana, Bea Kindly, Spirit of Mary, Claret And Blues, Liveadream, Enemy Action, Eevee Star, Inns And Out, and Mardy Bum — creates a significant redistribution problem; several of these are genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded, but in reality they will be bunched in a pack with no true pace to chase, making late momentum difficult to generate. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or tracking profile — horses who can be placed just off Lady Dublin's shoulder and kick at the 2f pole, rather than those relying on a strong pace to close into from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Dublin Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin finds a clean lead from stall and meets no early pressure, setting a measured but winning tempo.
scenarios.body: Lady Dublin dictates an uncontested, comfortable gallop from the front, never forced to over-exert, and the Good ground suits her recent winning form over this course and distance combination; with no genuine front-runner to challenge her she can conserve energy and accelerate again late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Lairy Mary and Crystal Kraken track Lady Dublin closely and one pounces as Lady Dublin flattens inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With pace steady rather than fierce, the two prominent types sitting just off the leader get an ideal stalking trip and can challenge in a 3-way finish from the 1f pole; Lairy Mary's course-winning form over 5f on Good and her prominent style make her the most likely beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Split Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and creates enough of a gap for the true hold-up horses to close through a tiring field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Enemy Action and Mardy Bum, two of the more authentic hold-up types who avoided redistribution issues, would be best placed to pounce late if fractions are genuinely testing; however, this scenario is tempered by the reality that several redistributed horses (Liveadream, Claret And Blues) racing out of their natural role reduce the depth of the late-closing threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-race incident or stumble causes Lady Dublin to lose her rhythm and the race devolves into a scramble from 2f out with no horse gaining a clean run.
scenarios.body: A messy, congested finish would suit horses with the widest draw or cleanest passage rather than any specific style profile; the overcrowded midfield pack would face traffic issues, making this the least predictable and least likely shape given Lady Dublin's straightforward recent course form.

watchPoints.text: Lady Dublin (stall/draw watch) — if she breaks cleanly and clears to the front without interference, her uncontested lead in a field with no other front-runner makes her the horse to beat throughout.

Lairy Mary — Tim Easterby's in-form stable (T14: 8/68) and a course win last time on Good suggest she could stalk Lady Dublin into a prominent challenge; watch how quickly Fentiman positions her in the first furlong.

Enemy Action and Mardy Bum — both are genuine hold-up types (not redistributed) who are fit and course-proven on Good; if the pace is stronger than expected, these two are the most credible threats from off the pace and worth tracking from the 2f pole.

Redistributed hold-up runners (Trust Havana, Claret And Blues, Liveadream, Spirit of Mary, Bea Kindly) — five horses racing out of their natural style create a significant congestion risk in the midfield pack; watch for traffic issues and blocked runs in the straight that could skew finishing positions.

races.name: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old veteran hold-up performer for Tim Easterby, Jake Dickson takes the ride claiming 5lb; his recent handicap form includes an eighth over 1m6f Good and a third over 1m4f Soft, and while the trip is familiar the form figures of 606038 suggest he needs things to fall perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Gibside's third two starts back stands out in an otherwise workmanlike sequence, and he has already run over today's trip and going. Yet to win in recent starts, he owns the fastest figure of this quintet and gets the vote after a 27-day break, that patchy placing record the main query.

runners_data.name: Tupero
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's lightly-burdened four-year-old carries a tpband and returns after 54 days off, but his two wins in last five outings over 1m4f-1m6f Good underline his ability to lead and repel rivals; Mark Winn partners him and the uncontested lead is his for the taking in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Tupero won last time out and has three wins in his last six starts, though he was only fourth four starts back and returns from a 54-day break. He has run over today's trip and going before, but sits bottom of our figures on a middling speed figure, hard to fancy on that alone.

runners_data.name: Port George
runners_data.note: 325 days off the track is a major query for this four-year-old from the Greenall & Guerriero yard, and his placing second over 1m4f Good last time out hints at ability when fresh; his natural instinct is to race from well off the pace, though the cluster of hold-up types here means he is likely to find himself forced into a more prominent position than suits.|
runners_data.comment: Port George was sixth last time out but had been runner-up three starts back, and he has run over today's going before. A 325-day absence since that last outing and a modest speed figure make him hard to fully trust, though that placed effort three starts back is the case for respect as a danger.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Approach
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's lightly-weighted three-year-old has won twice over 1m4f Good and placed twice more over similar trips, with Jason Hart booked and only 13 days since his last run — he races from behind and his class edge over the older rivals here could prove decisive if the pace is genuinely contested.|
runners_data.comment: Gaelic Approach was only sixth last time out, but he'd won four starts back and again six starts back. He has already run over today's trip and going, returns after just 13 days, and tops our figures here, making him the danger to beat despite that below-par latest effort.

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's four-year-old placed over 1m4f Good and 1m6f Good in his last three staying starts and is 15 days fresh; a natural closer by inclination, the reality of this field means he ends up mapping further forward than he would choose, though his best efforts have come when racing patiently rather than being asked to race prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Twilight Safari was fourth last time out and third two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going already banked. Yet to win in recent starts, he rates markedly higher with us than his official mark suggests, and returns after just 15 days as one of the leading dangers here.

races.paceDynamic: Tupero is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good ground at Thirsk. The remainder of the field — Gibside, Gaelic Approach, Port George, and Twilight Safari — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Tupero's lead will go uncontested and the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. Port George and Twilight Safari are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to a midfield position on the map simply because the field is stacked with closers and they cannot all sit at the back; in reality this field holds more off-the-pace types than can realistically be separated at the rear, with Tupero virtually certain to secure the front position unchallenged. A lone front-runner setting a measured tempo over a staying trip on Good ground creates a race that strongly favours resolute hold-up horses with a powerful late finish — provided they can close the gap Tupero has in hand — but the absence of genuine pace pressure equally allows Tupero to conserve energy and potentially control the tempo right to the line, meaning a well-rated, settled front-runner with tactical intelligence could prove very difficult to peg back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tupero Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tupero bowls along at a controlled clip, conserves energy through the false pace, and has enough in reserve to repel late challengers in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival pressing for the lead, Tupero can dictate every yard at a gallop that suits him, and his recent winning form over similar distances on Good ground underlines his ability to see out this trip when fresh.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just slow enough to bunch the field, allowing the best-credentialled hold-up horses to close with a sustained run in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Gaelic Approach's strong recent form over 1m4f-1m6f on Good ground and a capable conditional in the saddle in Jason Hart make him the most likely beneficiary if Tupero's front-running energy is spent too early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If Tupero is able to inject a decisive mid-race surge that stretches the field and leaves the redistributed hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Port George and Twilight Safari, both true hold-up types shuffled toward midfield by the field composition rather than by choice, would struggle to pick up if the race develops into a stop-start sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops in a chaotic fashion with horses unable to find their natural rhythm, allowing a lower-rated runner to benefit from a fortuitous position.
scenarios.body: Twilight Safari has shown ability at staying trips and has placed over 1m6f-2m1f on Good ground, so a muddled race where positional chaos negates class could bring him into play at long odds.

watchPoints.text: Tupero has a completely uncontested lead — watch whether Mark Winn exploits this by slowing the pace to a crawl in the back straight, effectively turning this into a sprint finish from 2f out which would neutralise the hold-up horses entirely.

Gaelic Approach has run six days ago over a shorter trip; Jason Hart may need to make a forward move earlier than ideal to avoid being blocked by the redistributed midfield runners, which could cost him momentum at a crucial stage.

Port George returns from 325 days off the track — watch his early behaviour and whether he settles into a rhythm, as a ring-rusty run could see him lose his position and fail to reach his natural hold-up berth at all.

With four genuine hold-up types in a five-runner field, watch for a bunched group tracking Tupero — if they fail to spread out through the final bend, interference in the short Thirsk straight becomes a live risk.

Twilight Safari's jockey Aiden Brookes should watch Gaelic Approach's move as a timing cue — if Brookes follows that run rather than going independently, Twilight Safari's finish may be compromised by traffic behind the more prominent types.

races.name: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has finished placed in 8 of 15 runs on Good ground including two wins, but her visor (hg:v) and a run just 2 days ago raise freshness concerns; she will fight hard for early position behind Zooella but her recent form string (521033) shows she is finding it harder to win at this level.
runners_data.comment: Miss Rainbow was third last time out and third again two starts back, with a win four starts back also in the book. She has already run over today's trip and going, is out again quickly just two days later, but sits near the foot of our figures in this nine-runner field.

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: John Butler has hit 4/10 in the last 14 days and Alistair Rawlinson rides, but Love Alive's hold-up style produces just 1 placed run from 11 on similar going with no wins; stepping from 5f to 6f is a positive trip change but the form string (159630) is unconvincing at this level.
runners_data.comment: Love Alive was unplaced last time out but had been third two starts back, with a win six starts back now some way in the past. She has already run over today's trip and going, returns after a 29-day break, and sits towards the foot of our figures, those indifferent recent efforts the main knock.

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond sends her back quickly (6 days) with 3 wins from 13 in the yard's recent period; a genuine hold-up type by nature, she is mapped to midfield here only because the rear of this field is saturated with hold-up horses, meaning she is racing structurally out of her preferred position and her chance should be discounted accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Oasis Cover was eighth last time out but had finished runner-up two starts back, a swing that sums up an inconsistent recent record. Yet to win in recent starts and bottom of our figures in this nine-runner field, she's quick to back up after just six days but has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey fit the p headgear for the first time and return her after 13 days, which is worth noting from a high-volume yard; her hold-up style has managed 1 win and 2 places from 9 runs on Good ground, and her best form at 6f on Good (5th last time) suggests she needs things to fall right late.
runners_data.comment: Eartha was fifth last time out, having also finished ninth two starts back and unplaced three starts back. Yet to win in recent starts, she tops our figures well above her official mark, and with experience over today's trip and going banked, returns as the biggest threat here after just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' consistent mare has placed in 7 of 15 runs on Good ground and finished second in her last five 6f runs — the most striking form line in the race; Jason Hart takes the ride and her prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Zooella, though she has yet to convert her consistency into a win at this OR.
runners_data.comment: Taygar was runner-up last time out and has been placed in four of her last five starts, a picture of real consistency for a mare still yet to win. She has already run over today's trip and going, quick to back up again after just 11 days, and remains one of the leading dangers on figures despite that stubborn lack of a win.

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's three-year-old has only four career runs but has placed in 3 of 4 on Good/Standard ground, and a prominent style over 6f at Thirsk suits; Ryan Sexton rides and the yard is 1/15 in the last fortnight, which tempers enthusiasm slightly despite an encouraging form profile.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Arrow was runner-up last time out and again two starts back, with a third four starts back showing further consistency, though a win remains elusive. She has run over today's distance before, returns after 23 days, and sits right in the mix on our figures, that missing win her only query.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) rides, but Ziggy's Queen races off the pace with a hood (hg:ht) and has no wins or places in 15 runs on Good ground — a structural disadvantage when the dominant shape favours those who travel prominently; her last five runs have all been over 7f, making the step to 6f a further concern.
runners_data.comment: Ziggy's Queen was only sixth last time out, with a win six starts back the highlight of a mixed sequence since. She has already run over today's trip and going, owns the fastest speed figure in this field, and returns after just 16 days as one of the leading dangers, that indifferent recent form the one query.

runners_data.name: Zooella
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan steers for Ralph Beckett (12/43 last 14 days, strong yard in form) and Zooella is the only confirmed front-runner in a 9-runner field; her last run was a 6f win at Sandown and she is on Quick back on turf, but the question is whether four prominent chasers apply enough pressure to eventually wear her down.
runners_data.comment: Zooella won last time out and has been in the frame in four of her last five starts, with experience over today's distance banked. Her trainer is in good form at 28% over the last fortnight, and she's out again quickly after just 11 days, making her the pick on profile even without topping our figures outright.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old has won 2 and placed 5 times in 15 Good-ground runs and carries the top weight (138lbs) as a prominent type; her best form is over 5f and stepping to 6f here means she may find the trip stretching her, though she will be competitive early if she can settle just off Zooella.
runners_data.comment: Canaria Queen was fifth last time out and fifth again two starts back, a poor spell sandwiched between much better placed form further back including a win three starts back. She has already run over today's trip and going, returns after 18 days, and sits mid-pack on our figures, that recent dip in form the obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Zooella is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Rossa Ryan aboard for Ralph Beckett's in-form yard (12/43 in the last 14 days), she is likely to be allowed to bowl along at a measured, sustainable tempo on Good ground over 6f at Thirsk. Behind her, Miss Rainbow, Taygar, Celtic Arrow, and Canaria Queen all want prominent positions, creating a congested early battle for the two or three berths just off the lead — the real race for position happens in the first two furlongs, with traffic danger likely between the 2f and 3f markers as this bunch sorts itself out. Hold-up runners Eartha, Ziggy's Queen, and Love Alive sit at the tail of the field by default, though Ziggy's Queen's hold-up style on a track that suits front-runners is a structural disadvantage; Oasis Cover is a genuine hold-up type but has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already crowded with true hold-up horses unlikely to get clear passage. The race shape strongly favours horses able to travel prominently in the slipstream of Zooella — a controlled front-running pace with moderate pressure from a pack of prominent types means the winner is most likely to come from those who settle just behind the leader and pick up smoothly, rather than from hold-up horses who will need a strong pace to close into. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their position cleanly — Taygar's course-record consistency on Good ground and Celtic Arrow's recent form give them the best chance of actually securing the prime seats behind Zooella; Canaria Queen, stepping up from 5f, may find the early pace duel costly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Zooella sets a fair but unsustainable gallop and the prominent horses settle cleanly 1-2 lengths off the pace, one of the prominently-placed chasers picks her off inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Zooella dictates from the front at a measured clip and the pack behind her avoids the worst of the early traffic, allowing the best-placed prominent horse to reel her in as she ties in the final 100 yards; Taygar's seven places in fifteen runs on Good ground and relentless 6f form make her the prime beneficiary of this shape, while Celtic Arrow's late kick is equally well-suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion behind Zooella causes interference and the hold-up horses are trapped wide or blocked, Zooella's controlled front-running proves good enough to last home.
scenarios.body: With rivals tied up in traffic battles from the 3f pole, Zooella is never headed and Rossa Ryan simply presses the button to stretch clear; Beckett's consistent record in the last fortnight supports the trainer angle, and a Good 6f at Thirsk suits a horse who has already won here at the track on a similar surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion turns into a genuine pace war with Miss Rainbow and Canaria Queen pushing Zooella hard from the off, the pace collapses late and a hold-up horse finishes fastest.
scenarios.body: A truly run race burns off the front-runners inside the final 2f, opening a window for Eartha or Love Alive to swoop, though both have moderate recent form and Love Alive has no wins in 11 runs on similar going; this scenario is constrained by the fact that most true hold-up runners in this field have limited winning form in these conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Traffic Avoidance
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders are tied up and a midfield runner avoids trouble by tracking widest, they emerge with a decisive run through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Oasis Cover, though racing out of her natural hold-up role, could benefit if she secures a clean line outside the scrimmage, though the STYLE_FIT discount and redistribution mean this is a low-probability path; Eartha's headgear change (p) and trainer angle give her a marginal claim if the race falls apart in front of her.

watchPoints.text: Taygar's five consecutive second-place finishes over 6f on Good ground make her the most dangerous prominent horse to Zooella — watch whether Jason Hart can secure a clear position directly behind the leader by the 4f pole.

The early duel for prominent positions between Miss Rainbow, Taygar, Celtic Arrow, and Canaria Queen creates a genuine interference risk between the 2f and 3f markers — any of these four could be badly hampered or forced wide before the race truly begins.

Zooella's solo front-running role is central to this race shape — if Canaria Queen or Miss Rainbow press her aggressively from the off rather than sitting in behind, the pace lifts and opens the door for hold-up runners Eartha and Love Alive much earlier than expected.

Ziggy's Queen's switch from 7f to 6f combined with a hold-up style and no Good-ground placed runs in 15 attempts makes her highly unlikely to feature under this race shape — watch Ethan Tindall's reaction if she is checked in the early traffic.

Ralph Beckett's yard is in excellent form (12/43 in 14 days) and Rossa Ryan is a key booking — the trainer-jockey combination is worth monitoring in the paddock for Zooella's demeanour ahead of her attempt to lead throughout.

races.name: JW4x4 Northallerton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with sound good-ground form (13 from 15 qualifiers) over this trip, though the sim-going win rate of four wins from five in good conditions is encouraging — needs Max Of Stars to set a strong enough tempo to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Sixty Plus was sixth last time out and sixth again three starts back, with a seventh in between. He has run over today's trip and going before, is with a yard in fine form at 34% over the last fortnight, and owns a strong speed figure that hints at more despite being yet to win.

runners_data.name: Wolf of Badenoch
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer who won over 11f on good ground recently and has placed at this sort of distance; Tom Culhane/Barclay yard has been quiet (1 from 4 in 14 days) but the horse's form figures suggest he is capable when conditions suit.|
runners_data.comment: Wolf of Badenoch won last time out, bouncing back from a below-par sixth two starts back to show he retains real ability. He has already run over today's trip and going, returns after just 15 days, and tops our figures comfortably in this five-runner field, with the patchy form further back the query.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a STYLE_FIT flag indicating he is racing out of natural role relative to this race map — yet here he is the natural leader, making that flag contextually reversed; strong sim-going record (12 from 15, 3W7P) and Ollie Pears yard in fair form (2 from 6, T14).|
runners_data.comment: Max Of Stars was runner-up last time out and third two starts back, with a win three starts back showing she has the class to trouble these. She has already run over today's trip and going, returns after 21 days, and is one of the leading dangers on figures, though a couple of below-par efforts further back temper the enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Solid performer on good ground with three wins from relevant conditions, but a true hold-up type whose redistribution to the midfield slot reflects overcrowding at the rear rather than a change of tactics — Harry Russell's brother Tom Eaves rides, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies if he cannot secure a forward berth.|
runners_data.comment: Dubai Venture won last time out and was also successful five starts back, either side of a moderate sixth two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, returns after 17 days, and though he's bottom of our figures here, a strong speed figure suggests he could yet play a hand.

runners_data.name: Educate
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning (0W 1P from 15 sim-going runs), running in cheekpieces (tv flag), and racing just 10 days after its last start for Micky Hammond who is in fair form (3 from 13 in 14 days) — a natural hold-up type pushed into the midfield slot on the map, and the form string of 565633 suggests placed efforts are the ceiling.|
runners_data.comment: Educate was third last time out and third again two starts back, a consistent recent sequence even without a win to show for it. He has run over today's trip and going before, backs up quickly after just 10 days, and rates well above his official mark, making him one of the leading dangers.

races.paceDynamic: Max Of Stars is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no rival likely to press him hard for the lead, he should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this 1m4f on good ground at Thirsk. Behind him, Sixty Plus and Wolf of Badenoch are both genuine hold-up horses who will need the pace to be honest enough to reel him in from off the bridle, while Dubai Venture and Educate are also natural hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because the rear is over-populated — neither is a natural stalker of the pace. The field effectively contains four horses who want to come from behind and one horse who wants to make the running, creating a scenario where the leader controls tempo and the closers have to hope it is genuinely run to suit them. This shape firmly favours a prominent or pace-stalking profile: Max Of Stars, dictating from the front, is best positioned to exploit a race run at a tempo of his own choosing, while the hold-up brigade face a tactical lottery if he keeps the pace modest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Max Stars Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars leads unchallenged and sets a controlled, honest gallop that he can sustain to the line.
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars, with no pressure from rivals, finds his rhythm on the front end and is never asked to go beyond his comfort zone, making a winning strike on his own terms at a pace the closers cannot bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to tire Max Of Stars inside the final two furlongs, allowing hold-up horses to swoopfrom off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Sixty Plus and Wolf of Badenoch, tracking wide of a fading front-runner, both have the good-ground form to finish powerfully if the gallop has been sufficient — Wolf of Badenoch's recent course-and-distance win gives him the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dubai Venture Stalks Through
scenarios.trigger: If Dubai Venture, despite being a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield, is ridden more prominently than usual and makes a decisive move rounding the home turn.
scenarios.body: Racing closer than his natural style dictates, Dubai Venture's strong form record on good ground over this sort of trip — three wins from relevant conditions — could prove decisive if he gets a favourable position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the race is unusually slowly run early and then develops into a sprint finish in which positional advantage is neutralised.
scenarios.body: With all four closers arriving in a bunch, the one with the most residual class and topspeed — Wolf of Badenoch on his best form — edges it in a tight photo, though this shape is the least likely given one lone, pace-setting type in the field.

watchPoints.text: Max Of Stars controls every key variable in this race — if Harry Russell simply dictates a moderate pace from the front, the closers' ability to close the gap diminishes sharply and his winning chance increases substantially.

Wolf of Badenoch's switch to a longer trip (recent win over 11f, now 1m4f) and good-ground profile makes him the most dangerous hold-up threat if he can get a clear run from off the pace — watch where Stevie Donohoe positions him leaving the stalls.

Dubai Venture and Educate are both flagged as redistributed hold-up types shown in midfield — if they are unable to secure their natural position and get bunched at the rear behind a slow pace, the closers' scenario becomes significantly harder to execute.

Sixty Plus has a strong sim-going hit rate (13 from 15 qualifiers) but has not won since a return to good ground suggests improvement — Rossa Ryan will need to time a late challenge perfectly given the lone front-runner scenario.

The headgear flag on Educate (cheekpieces, tv) combined with a 10-day turnaround is worth noting for market movers — Hammond's yard is active enough to flag if this signals an intended forward move in running style, though form says otherwise.

races.name: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Apprentice Training Race - Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears-trained hold-up performer placed on Good ground at 5f recently, but is a true rear-to-midfield type shifted forward on the map due to field congestion; STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence in the scenario needing a late run.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out is the highlight, but this filly is without a win in her last five and rates only 58, ranked seventh of these nine. She has run over today's trip and going before, though little else in the recent form marks her out.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has placed at 5f on Good before but has struggled for consistency, a natural hold-up runner who will be hemmed in behind horses who themselves want to come from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our rankings on a figure of 47, this filly does have a third four starts back but is without a win in her last five. She has run over today's trip and going before, though on these figures she has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a win in similar conditions on his record, genuine hold-up style that the map has pushed closer to midfield than is natural for him; trainer M&D Easterby hit 3/26 in 14 days which is modest.
runners_data.comment: A second last time out is the standout form, though this gelding is without a win in his last five and rates only 52, ranked eighth of these nine. He has run over today's trip and going before, but there is plenty more needed here.

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; six-year-old with 2W5P on Good and has won over this course and distance combination before, carrying a tongue tie and the most advantageous tactical position of anyone in the field.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out, and a winner five starts back, this gelding has otherwise been frequently in the frame. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 61 keeps him firmly in the pack rather than among the leaders.

runners_data.name: Mare Of London
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by Mark Walford who placed at 6f on Good last time, steps down to 5f here; true hold-up profile but maps closest to the prominent position and has place form at shorter, 18 days off is fresh but not concerning.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out, and a second four starts back, this filly is winless in her last five but ranks second of these nine on our figures. She has run over today's trip and going before, though the 18-day gap since her last outing is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Country Artiste
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's three-year-old has been well held in eight of the last twelve outings on similar ground; runs off a natural hold-up style and trainer has 0/10 in the 14-day window which removes any significant confidence angle.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last five starts and yet to find the frame, this filly does carry a workmanlike speed figure of 68. She has run over today's trip and going before, with a rating of 62 keeping her among the pack rather than the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Michael Dods horse with three places at 5f Good in recent history and the highest weight in the field at 138lbs; genuine hold-up type capable of finishing into the places if the pace is honest, 19 days since last run is routine.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, and a third three starts back, this gelding is winless in his last five but rates 64, marking him among the leading dangers. He has run over today's trip and going before, with the lack of a win the one query.

runners_data.name: Sunlit Sea
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old won at 5f Good on her most recent qualifying run and wears a blinker; a true hold-up runner that the map has advanced forward — the visor aids concentration but the redistribution means she won't get her favoured off-the-pace position naturally.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, this filly carries our top rating of 65 and has run over today's trip and going before. Back within nine days of that success, she looks the one to beat, with a modest speed figure of 54 the main blot.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's eight-year-old with a strong recent record of 3P and 0W at 5f Good, wears a hood and is a natural hold-up performer pushed into the midfield portion of the map; Easterby's 8/68 strike rate in the last 14 days is active but the horse has not won in some time.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out, and a second two starts back, this gelding is yet to score in his last six starts but shows a strong speed figure of 71. He has run over today's trip and going before, though last time's dip to sixth is the one query.

races.paceDynamic: Irish Dancer is the sole confirmed front runner in this nine-runner sprint and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from the gates rather than being dragged into a war. The remainder of the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up and come-from-behind types, meaning the early fractions will be controlled rather than contested, and the pace Irish Dancer sets will likely be honest but not frenetic on Good ground over five furlongs at Thirsk. That relatively untroubled lead gives Irish Dancer a significant tactical advantage — she can dictate her own rhythm, avoid any early scrimmaging, and simply ask questions of her rivals two furlongs out. This race shape favours the horse on the front end and those able to travel prominently just off the pace, as horses coming from genuinely deep off a moderate gallop will need significant late ground that a comfortable leader rarely surrenders over five furlongs. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Albegone, Sunlit Sea, Dabbling, and Gwen Tennyson are all true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map, and Irish Dancer alongside Mare Of London are most likely to actually secure the positions closest to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Irish Dancer Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Irish Dancer jumps cleanly and establishes a comfortable lead inside the first furlong with no genuine pace rival to harass her.
scenarios.body: She controls fractions throughout, conserves energy through the middle section, and simply kicks clear from two furlongs out on Good ground she handles well — her record of 2W5P on similar going underpins this.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominents Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Irish Dancer sets a slightly quicker early pace than intended and those tracking just off her can sustain momentum to overhaul her close home.
scenarios.body: Horses able to sit two or three lengths off the leader and avoid the midfield traffic will pick up the pieces as Irish Dancer ties up in the final furlong; the Good surface keeps ground coming back to those with late kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If Irish Dancer burns out after setting a genuinely hot pace and the hold-up horses, despite racing further forward than ideal, find more room on the Good ground than anticipated.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of hold-up types into midfield means some of these horses will be closer than normal and in a strongly-run race could get home; Sunlit Sea's recent win on similar going gives her the profile to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, No Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate it bunches the field and creates a sprint-for-home scenario where draw, weight, and luck in running decide the outcome.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure, the field concertinas approaching the final two furlongs and any hold-up horse with a clean run and low weight becomes dangerous; Country Artiste and So Grateful hold big enough weights to make this harder.

watchPoints.text: Irish Dancer — the sole front-runner in the race, her ability to jump cleanly and establish an unchallenged lead before the field settles is the single biggest determinant of the race shape; watch her early.

Sunlit Sea — Prescott runners wearing headgear on a return to winning form are typically well-prepared, and despite being pushed forward on the map as a hold-up type, a clear run from midfield could make her dangerous in Scenarios B and C.

Midnight Lir — top weight at 138lbs could anchor her late, but three recent placed efforts at 5f Good show she handles this exact scenario; if Irish Dancer ties up, she is the natural beneficiary from just off the pace.

Albegone — hood-wearing, hold-up veteran who finds himself in a field where everyone wants the same back-of-the-pack ground; traffic and positioning in the straight will be critical, and a poor draw or slow break could cost her entirely.

Country Artiste — trainer at 0/10 in the last 14 days and consistently well-beaten on similar ground; mention only to note she is the most likely to be detached if the pace quickens, as her recent form lines offer no reason to expect improvement.
